div.head: Rect 8
div.ab: [8] Be manna metsunge. Anan esne gebyreð to metsunge XII pund godes cornes 7 II scipæteras 7 I god metecu, wuduræden be landside.
Uni æsno (id est inopi) contingunt ad uictum XII pondia bone annone et duo scæpeteras (id est ouium corpora) et I bona conuictualis uacca, esarticare iuxta situm terrę.
Be manna met|sunge . Anan esne gebyreð to metsunge . xii . pund godes cornes . 7 ii . scipæteras. 7 .i. god me|tecu wuduræden be landside.
Be manna metsunge Anan esne gebyreð to metsunge XII pund godes cornes and II scipæteras and I god metecu, wuduræden be landside.
Concerning the provisioning of men Each labourer is due as provisions, twelve pounds of good corn and two sheep carcasses and one good food cow [and] an arrangement to gather wood.

Regarding the Feeding of the Men For his food, each laborer is due twelve pounds of good grain, two sheep carcasses, one cow for meat, and an arrangement for gathering wood according to the local custom.

Von Beköstigung der männlichen [Hörigen]. Je einem Knechte gebührt als [jährliche] Beköstigung 12 ‘Pfund’ [genannte Getreidelasten] guten Korns und 2 Schaf[leiber?] und 1 gute Nährkuh, Holz[fällung]recht nach Gutsbrauch.

Of the food allowance of [unfree] men. To each slave is due as [yearly] food allowance 12 ‘pounds’ [i.e. loads] of good grain and 2 sheep[-carcasses?] and 1 good food-cow, and wood[-cutting] right according to the custom of the estate.
div.note: Liebermann notes that by the custom of Gloucester the customary tenant received for mowing one sheep-carcass (Vinogradoff), at Borley in 1308 a ‘hurtardum’ when the customary tenants mowed. The Quadripartitus's ‘esarticare’ (to clear land, French essarter) is inexact; the assonance misled it (correct is ‘iuxta’ as in 4.4). Liebermann compares 12.1 and 13.1.
